controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Uúba; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of LTT 9779 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of ltt-9779's light, as its color dataset measures it.

controls.label: Spitzer
controls.qualification: Published fit · Crossfield et al. (2020) · a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 14290) · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature at 4.5 µm of LTT 9779 b from Crossfield et al. (2020)'s published fit to a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 14290). Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 10° west of noon. Longitudes where the fit gives no emission are left blank. The false color runs from 400 to 1,950 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of Uúba's planets in this map from above, to scale, with LTT 9779 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

LTT 9779 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (69, 96, 106) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 183985250, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 4-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
